messages:
Maya: Quick heads-up — after the kernel v11 adaptive toggle landed we saw ~12% drop in KV prefix hit-rate on beta traffic and a couple GPU OOMs in staging. Anyone else seeing this?
Devin: I noticed it in the overnight perf run. CPU->GPU cache ratio moved and eviction counts spiked. 99p token latency increased. Perf dump: https://internal.storage/perf/2079990000/trace.html
Leo: pinging @Samar and infra-bot for deploy metadata. Could be batch heuristic + kernel route interaction causing KV prefill to be skipped.
infra-bot: deploy v11.2.0 rolled to canary @ 2079989400. No autoscaler events during the canary window.
Samar: I changed soft-ttl aggressiveness from 1.0 -> 0.8 last night to cut compaction work. Heatmap shows more small-slot fragmentation (avg slot size 1.9 -> 1.2). Eviction seems to favor newer keys now, possibly evicting long-tail prefixes quicker.
Maya: Quick numbers from the cache profiler (summarized): total_keys=1.2M, prefix_hit 58% -> 46%, avg_warmup_per_prefix 230ms -> 340ms, GPU_free -6%.
Devin: Hypothesis: kernel selection now prefers matmul-kernel-B for short sequences; that scheduler path bypasses the KV prefill hook, so prefixes arrive cold.
Leo: Can you dump the kernel decision trace? I remember a test flag `--force-kernel-b` used in perf runs.
Devin: Pasted the sampling config I used:
```text
# sampling config
warmup:
  enable: true
  prefill_window_ms: 120
  prefill_strategy: cohort
kv:
  soft_ttl_ratio: 0.8
  eviction: lru
kernel:
  selection_mode: adaptive
  prefer_small_seq: true
```
Samar: That aligns with what I saw. If the scheduler route bypasses prefill hooks we will see slower warmup and lower hit-rate. Mitigation: add a prefill hook at the common scheduler entry before kernel dispatch.
Maya: Proposed patch: call `prefill.on_request()` from the common scheduler entrypoint (before kernel selection). Minimal change but ensures prefill runs regardless of kernel path.
Leo: Risk: extra overhead on the hot path. But acceptable to canary. Also suggest temporarily raising `gpu_soft_limit` by +8% to avoid OOMs during test.
Devin: I'll create a canary with two diffs: (1) prefill-hook in scheduler, (2) bump `gpu_soft_limit` 0.84 -> 0.92.
Samar: I'll queue synthetic prefix-heavy perf runs. Also prototyping LRU aging tweak: reduce recency weight so long-tail prefixes survive longer.
infra-bot: perf job #742 queued. ETA ~40m.
Maya: Also add metric `kv.prefill.bypassed_by_kernel` and `kv.prefill.latency_ms` so we can validate the hypothesis.
Devin: One more note — batch size heuristics interacting with kernel-B produced ~14% drop in tokens_per_batch on beta, which can slow warmup throughput as well.
Leo: End-to-end checklist: 1) canary patch, 2) perf + trace, 3) compare `prefix_hit` and `tokens_per_batch`, 4) rollback if OOMs spike.
Samar: Tests queued against stage-2. I'll post results here. Also iterating a more conservative eviction weight.
Maya: Sounds good — keep updates here. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: perf job #742 completed at 2079990360. Summary: prefix_hit +7% vs canary baseline, tokens_per_batch +3%, OOMs down. Full results: https://internal.storage/perf/742/results
Devin: Promising but not full recovery. We'll need follow-ups (kernel-aware prefill optimizations and batch heuristic tuning).
Leo: I'm +1 for staged rollout with close monitoring.
Samar: Deploying the patch to stage-2 at 2079990300; monitoring dashboards enabled.
Maya: Acknowledged — watching alerts and `kv.prefill.*` metrics now.
